messages:
maria: perf-bot alert — kv-prefix cache hit-rate collapsed in rw-inference-prod (us-west-2). 92% -> ~4% in the last 10m, 99p latency x3. grafana: https://grafana.redwood/prod/kv-cache

owen: joining. which model/variant and which pool? any recent infra changes?

perf-bot: alert details: model=redwood/open-13b-v2-quant, pool=prod-pool-usw2, affected_pods=14/48, kv_eviction_rate spike at 2024-12-05T02:40Z

jana: we shipped kernel-selection v3 + batch-heuristic tweak yesterday (rollout 02:15 UTC). change favored fused-attn kernels and larger micro-batches on A100 nodes. also updated kv key composition in runtime code for tracing.

kevin: looking at pod logs (quick grep):
```
kubectl -n prod logs rw-infer-22 | grep kv_cache_evicted | tail -n 50
2024-12-05T02:41:05Z kv_cache_evicted=True prefix_hash=0x1a3f4
2024-12-05T02:41:05Z kv_cache_evicted=True prefix_hash=0x1a3f4
... many repeats ...
```
Shows repeated evictions and immediate misses. memory reclaim events on node-5 around same time.

owen: repeated evictions + new nodes = cold caches => cascaded misses. any code change that could make cache keys unique per request? that would be cache poisoning.

jana: oh dang — i pushed a small trace change in runtime/kv_cache.py that accidentally included request_id in the prefix key for debug: 
```
- key = f"{model}:{prefix_hash}"
+ key = f"{model}:{prefix_hash}:{request_id}"  # oops
```
That would make every request unique and bypass shared prefix caching. I thought it was behind a flag but looks like it landed.

maria: that matches the timing exactly. perf-bot shows the decline starting 02:15 when the deploy finished.

deploy-bot: rollout v3 completed 2024-12-05T02:15Z (changes: kernel-selection v3, batch-heuristic v2, kv-key-trace).

kevin: autoscaler reacted to latency by adding nodes. new nodes came up empty so hit-rate dropped even further (cold starts). autoscaler config allowed rapid scaling => amplify.

owen: mitigation plan: 1) rollback kv key change (fast), 2) throttle autoscaler scale-ups for 10m to avoid cold-node cascade, 3) run cache-prefill job to warm new pods. Who can push the rollback?

jana: i can revert and push a patch now. prepping PR with fix and a unit test to ensure request_id is not part of cache key.

maria: staging canary first? push to 10% then monitor kv-hit-rate, 99p latency. if green, roll to 100%.

jana: pushed fix -> PR #4829, rolling canary to 10% in prod-pool-usw2.

perf-bot: canary metrics (5m after patch): kv-hit-rate on canary pods=86%, baseline pods still ~6%. 99p latency on canary down ~30%.

owen: good signal. start progressive rollout to 50% then 100% with 5m watch windows. also pause autoscaler during rollout (kevin do you have perms?).

kevin: paused autoscaler for prod-pool-usw2 for 12m. scaling paused. continuing rollout to 100% now.

perf-bot: after full rollout (10m): cluster kv-hit-rate stabilized at 88%, 99p latency back to normal. evictions per-minute dropped to baseline.

maria: root cause summary: accidental inclusion of request_id in kv prefix key (cache poisoning) combined with autoscaler-driven cold nodes and a batch/kernel rollout that changed memory/latency profile -> cascade.

jana: follow-ups: add CI test to assert cache key composition, gate debug/tracing changes behind runtime flag, add alert for sudden kv-hit-rate deltas (>20% drop in 5m), add a prefill hook when autoscaler adds nodes.

maria: also write postmortem and link PRs. thanks all for fast response :heart:

owen: thumbs up. can someone add the incident to postmortems/ with timeline and impact numbers?

kevin: i'll draft the incident page and include heap profiles, kubectl dumps, and the offending commit.

perf-bot: incident resolved — monitoring for 1h.

maria: closing slack thread, moving to postmortem doc.
